S No or directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  ABA 694/2023  Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, Advocate, for the applicant.
Mr. Ranjan Ghildiyal, AGA, for the State.

(2) Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with FIR No. 395 of 2023, under Section 420 IPC,
registered with PS Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar.
(3) Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is serving as Senior Branch Manager with United Insurance Company.
It is contended that the only allegation against the applicant in the FIR is that he acted beyond his powers in settling the claims of cashless insurance policies.

It is also contended that maximum jail sentence for the alleged offence is up to seven years, therefore,
applicant is entitled to benefit of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar vs.
State of Bihar and another, reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273, followed in Md. Asfak Alam v. State of Jharkhand, reported in 2023 SCC OnLine SC 892.

sentences.text:
(4) Learned State Counsel fairly submits that since the offence is punishable with maximum jail sentence of up to seven years, therefore,
Investigating Officer shall give notice to the applicant in terms of Section 41-A of CrPC and subject to his complying with the conditions of said notice, applicant shall not be arrested.
( 5) With the consent of learned Counsel for the parties, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of by taking the statement made by learned State Counsel on record.
However, it is made clear that in case the applicant violates any condition of notice under Section 41- A of CrPC, I.O. shall be at liberty to proceed against the applicant as per law.

(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 19.8.2023 Pr ABA/694/2023 on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140648785/
